Codex review: found issues before merge. _Reviewed July 25, 2026, 9:50 AM ET / 13:50 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The branch replaces the Control UI observer HUD and detached `/btw` side chat with a dockable session rail backed by an ephemeral, read-only gateway companion thread, while adding OpenAI long-session cache-key clamps. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Needs maintainer review before merge - 6 items remain** Keep this PR open for maintainer review. It adds a substantial new Control UI and gateway capability with real behavior evidence, but the PR itself documents a remaining companion-answer leak into the main chat view that should be fixed before merge; the `maintainer` label and assignment also require explicit human handling. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `a4f67acb4a10c11a224699d74555a09df5fc14b5` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Strong user-path evidence supports a useful cross-layer implementation, but the acknowledged main-chat event leak blocks a higher correctness rating. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (screenshot): The PR supplies a concrete isolated live-Gateway scenario with observed timings and outcomes, sanitized wide/narrow/collapsed rail screenshots, and a successful repository real-behavior-proof check; the remaining merge blocker is the acknowledged event-isolation defect, not absent proof. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (screenshot): The PR supplies a concrete isolated live-Gateway scenario with observed timings and outcomes, sanitized wide/narrow/collapsed rail screenshots, and a successful repository real-behavior-proof check; the remaining merge blocker is the acknowledged event-isolation defect, not absent proof. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 5 items | Changed product boundary: The branch adds three public Gateway methods for companion asks, state retrieval, and reset, all scoped through the core gateway method registry; the Control UI then routes `/btw` and `/side` into the new rail instead of the detached side-chat path.
Documented remaining regression: The PR body explicitly records that a companion final answer can briefly flash in an open main chat view through an unkeyed live-event broadcast. That is a current, user-visible isolation defect in the submitted behavior, not a completed follow-up.
Real behavior evidence: The PR body reports isolated live Gateway runs for mid-run and idle questions, per-session switching, reload rehydration, and supplied sanitized rail screenshots; the provided checks list also shows the repository Real behavior proof check succeeded. | | **Findings** | 1 actionable finding | [P2] Keep companion answers out of the main chat stream | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Control UI chat connects directly to the Gateway and renders live session observer data alongside the conversation. This change adds per-session companion RPCs in the Gateway, then uses them from the chat rail to show bounded question-and-answer state without interrupting the main agent run. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Control UI chat] --> B[Session rail] B --> C[Gateway companion RPCs] C --> D[Read-only companion runner] D --> E[Target session history and workspace] D --> F[Bounded in-memory thread] F --> C C --> B B --> G[Operator-visible session answers] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should OpenClaw permanently expose the three session-companion Gateway RPCs and make Control UI `/btw` and `/side` use the bounded session companion rather than the detached BTW path? | **Approve the session-companion contract:** Keep the additive RPCs and Control UI rail after the main-chat event leak is fixed and the exact head completes required validation. | Why: This is a new cross-client Gateway contract and a deliberate Control UI command-semantics change; tests and proof can validate implementation quality but cannot choose the long-term product and compatibility boundary. ## Before merge - [ ] **Keep companion answers out of the main chat stream (P2)** - The PR description confirms that a completed companion answer can briefly flash in an open main chat through an unkeyed live event. The general chat-event handler must reject or key that event before it can update the main-agent view; otherwise operators can see assistant text that did not belong to the active conversation. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The submitted PR acknowledges that an answer from the companion can briefly render in the main chat through an unkeyed live-event path; this can confuse operators about what the main agent actually said. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The PR changes Control UI `/btw` and `/side` semantics and introduces three public Gateway methods with bounded session-scoped state, so maintainers should explicitly accept the compatibility and lifecycle contract before merging. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The branch is large and its remaining Android/iOS and CI lanes were still running or queued in the supplied check state; merge should wait for the exact head's required checks rather than treating the partial green set as final. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - The protected `maintainer` label and the remaining cross-layer event-isolation defect require human review on this PR rather than an automated repair lane. ## Findings - [P2] Keep companion answers out of the main chat stream — `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-gateway.ts:386-392`

A maintainer can ask Mantis to capture proof by posting this exact PR comment: ```text @openclaw-mantis web UI chat proof: reproduce a session-companion answer while the main chat is open and capture a redacted transcript showing the completion stays only in the session rail. ``` ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Fix main-chat event isolation first (recommended)** Ensure companion-run events are keyed and filtered so they cannot be rendered as a main-agent response, then revalidate the live rail flow. 2. **Accept the new Gateway and command contract** A maintainer can explicitly accept the additive RPC surface and Control UI `/btw` behavior change once the isolation defect is resolved. 3. **Pause the feature boundary** If a shared cross-client companion contract is not desired, pause this broad PR and retain the existing detached UI behavior.

### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep the session rail and companion as the single Control UI path, first prevent companion-run events from reaching the main chat stream, then obtain explicit maintainer acceptance of the new Gateway API and `/btw` compatibility boundary before merging. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes for the documented regression: keep a main chat view open, submit a companion question, and observe completion through the unkeyed live-event path; the PR body identifies this path and the changed chat gateway handler is the relevant receiving surface. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Unclear. Consolidating overlapping Control UI surfaces is coherent, but publishing new Gateway methods and changing `/btw` semantics is only the best solution if maintainers affirm that shared client contract after the main-chat event leak is fixed. Addressing the ClawSweeper before-merge items on head `94a7fcaff51d`:

- **Companion answers out of the main chat stream (P2 + P1)** — fixed in-branch. Root cause: internal-effects run events were routed with the sandbox session key (the visible parent) instead of the hidden transcript key (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-prepare.ts`). A headless gateway WS capture now shows zero main-keyed answer-bearing events; regression tests added at the emitter (4/4) and in the UI terminal-event guard (`chat-gateway.test.ts`). The UI also now requires a real run id for sessionless terminal events, closing an `undefined === undefined` fallback hole.
- **Contract acceptance (P1)** — the three additive `sessions.companion.*` methods and the Control UI `/btw`/`/side` rail routing implement the maintainer's explicit design direction for this feature; `sessions.observer.ask` (Android) and the TUI `/btw` path are intentionally untouched, with migrations tracked as follow-ups.
- **Exact-head checks (P1)** — the previous head went green after a rerun of one unrelated `ENOTEMPTY` tmp-cleanup flake; CI is running on this head now and landing waits for it.
